newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK Dec industrial output to bounce back.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK Dec industrial output to bounce back.

text.p: UK industrial and manufacturing output data for December, due at 0930 GMT Thursday, should show a return to a more stable upward trend after a shock fall in November, analysts said.
Output should have remained relatively resistant to sterling's strength during that month, although the currency's spirited gains may have take the shine off industry output figures soon after.
"I don't believe that November's unexpected fall signalled that start of a period of sustained weakness because of the strength of the pound," said HSBC economist Jonathan Loynes.
"It was rather more of an erratic fall. It is too early to have seen the effect of the pound yet."
A poll conducted by Reuters suggested industrial production rose 0.5 percent month-on-month in December for a 1.3 percent year-on- year, unchanged from November.
December manufacturing output is forecast to rise 0.3 percent on the month for a 1.1 percent gain on the year compared with November's 0.2 percent annual rise.

Sterling has gained around seven percent on a trade-weighted basis over the past six months, and since more than 50 percent of Britain's manufacturing output ends up overseas, analysts say the effect is bound to seep through at some stage.
"It is still not clear whether the impact of sterling's recent strength has fed through," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International in London.

"We are expecting a slight rebound from November, but it will be consistent with a sluggish pick-up in the manufacturing sector," he said, adding he forecast only a 0.1 percent month- on-month rise in manufacturing output.

While the latest Confederation of British Industry (CBI) survey showed that manufacturing output grew steadily over the past four months, it said sterling's strength may be starting to erode demand for exports.
"Clearly sterling continues to be a factor," said Mark Miller of Morgan Stanley. "But I am looking looking for a modest recovery (in output) from November."
Michael Saunders, economist at Salomon Brothers, said he expected November's blip down to be reversed.
"The recent CBI survey suggested that fourth quarter manufacturing output expanded at a similar pace to the third quarter," he said.
"Given that the average level of manufacturing output in October and November was 0.25 percent -- above the third-quarter average -- we expect a rebound in December."
Both Saunders and Stamenkovic said December's uncharacteristically cold weather could boost industrial figures due to an expected surge in output in the utilities sector.
This, Stamenkovic said, would go some way towards balancing out any sterling-initiated weakness in manufacturing.
